variable.title: General Contact sender name
variable.summary: The name messages sent from the General Contact identity appear to come from.
variable.origin: Stored in the configuration under Stores > Configuration > General > Store Email Addresses > General Contact. Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::configDirective reads it through the scope configuration for the store view the message is sent in.
variable.caveat: The value can differ per store view, so check the scope switcher on the configuration page before deciding the value is wrong.

variable.title: General Contact sender address
variable.summary: The email address messages sent from the General Contact identity are sent from.
variable.origin: Stored in the configuration under Stores > Configuration > General > Store Email Addresses > General Contact. Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::configDirective reads it through the scope configuration for the store view the message is sent in.
variable.caveat: The address is checked when it is saved by Magento\Config\Model\Config\Backend\Email\Address, so a value that is not an email address is refused rather than stored.
The value can differ per store view. The scope named beside the editor is the one that will be written.

variable.title: Email stylesheet
variable.summary: The stylesheet the message carries in its head, taken from the current theme.
variable.origin: The directive loads the named stylesheet from the theme the message is rendered with, compiles it, and puts the result where the directive stands. In the default theme the source of this file is web/css/email.less.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Copy the stylesheet into your own theme, under web/css/ in the theme directory.
Edit the copy. A file in the theme takes precedence over the one the theme inherits.
Deploy static content so the change reaches the next message that is sent.

variable.caveat: In a plain-text template the directive produces nothing at all.
When the file cannot be loaded, or compiles to nothing, the directive leaves a CSS comment in the message rather than reporting an error.

variable.title: Store view id, written as a method call
variable.summary: This does not print the store view id. On a standard installation it prints nothing at all.
variable.origin: A path inside {{var}} is never a method call. getId() is read as a request for an id value held on the store object, and the store record carries store_id rather than id, so the path comes back empty.

affordance.label: What to write instead
affordance.step: Write {{var store.store_id}}, which reads the value the store record actually carries.

variable.caveat: Nothing reports this. The directive is replaced by an empty string.

variable.title: Store view id
variable.summary: The numeric identifier of the store view the message is being sent for.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate puts the store view the message is being sent for into the template variables under the name store, and store_id is a column of the store record it carries.

affordance.label: Where this value comes from
affordance.step: A store view keeps the id it was given when it was created. Nothing in the administration changes it.
The store views on this installation are listed under Stores, All Stores.

variable.caveat: The id is a database key rather than anything an administrator chose, so it means nothing to a recipient.

variable.title: The {{var}} directive
variable.summary: Prints a value the code that sends the message put into the template, such as a field of the order, of the customer or of the store view.
variable.origin: The name inside the directive is a path into the values the sending code assigned to the template: the first part names one of those values and each part after a full stop reads something out of it.

affordance.label: How to change what this prints
affordance.step: To print something else, pick another variable from the variable chooser. That list is what the code sending this particular message makes available; a name that is not on it prints nothing.
To change how it is printed, use the formatting controls in this panel rather than typing after the vertical bar, so that only the formatting is rewritten.
To change the value itself, change the record it is read from - the order, the customer, the store configuration. Nothing in the template writes it.

variable.caveat: In an email template a {{var}} directive with no vertical bar in it is escaped as HTML. That comes from the email template filter rather than from the directive: text run through Magento\Framework\Filter\Template on its own - the store address layout, for one - gets no escaping at all, so the rule cannot be carried over to templates outside email.

Only escape and nl2br are implemented. Everything after the first vertical bar is read as the formatting, and a name that is neither of those two is skipped without a word. That is the whole of how |raw works, and it is also why a misspelling such as |rwa switches the escaping off just as effectively.

The argument of escape is matched exactly, and the three it accepts are html, htmlentities and url. |escape:HTML matches none of them and the value comes back unescaped, so it does the opposite of what it looks like it is asking for.

A part of the path written with brackets after it is not a method call. store.getFrontendName() is read as a request for the frontend_name value held on the store object, and a name that does not begin with get is not read at all, so {{var store.isActive()}} prints nothing.
When a message is rendered with no template variables assigned at all, the directive is left in the output exactly as it was written instead of being replaced.

variable.title: The {{config}} directive
variable.summary: Prints the value of one store configuration setting, read for the store view the message is sent in.
variable.origin: The directive reads the configuration path named by its path parameter while the message is being rendered, for the store view it is sent in, so a store view value overrides the website value, which overrides the default.

affordance.label: How to make another setting readable
affordance.step: The list of readable paths is a dependency injection argument of Magento\Variable\Model\Config\Structure\AvailableVariables. No admin page changes it.
In a module of your own, add an item for the path to that argument, grouped under the configuration group it belongs to, exactly as Magento_Variable does for the paths below.
Flush the configuration cache; until then the directive keeps rendering as an empty string.

variable.caveat: A {{config}} directive reads twenty-two paths and no others: web/unsecure/base_url, web/secure/base_url, trans_email/ident_general/name, trans_email/ident_general/email, trans_email/ident_sales/name, trans_email/ident_sales/email, trans_email/ident_support/name, trans_email/ident_support/email, trans_email/ident_custom1/name, trans_email/ident_custom1/email, trans_email/ident_custom2/name, trans_email/ident_custom2/email, general/store_information/name, general/store_information/phone, general/store_information/hours, general/store_information/country_id, general/store_information/region_id, general/store_information/postcode, general/store_information/city, general/store_information/street_line1, general/store_information/street_line2 and general/store_information/merchant_vat_number.

Any other path renders as an empty string. Nothing is logged and nothing is shown, so a directive naming a perfectly real setting that is not on the list looks exactly like a setting that has no value.

This directive takes no formatting. A vertical bar written inside it is either dropped, or - if the path is not in quotation marks - becomes part of the path, which then matches nothing and renders as an empty string.

variable.title: The {{customVar}} directive
variable.summary: Prints one of the custom variables kept under System > Other Settings > Custom Variables.
variable.origin: The directive loads the variable whose code its code parameter names, for the store view the message is sent in, and prints its HTML value in an HTML message and its plain value in a plain-text one.
variable.caveat: A variable with no HTML value is not empty in an HTML message: the plain value is printed instead, with its HTML escaped and its line breaks turned into br tags. So markup typed into the plain value appears in the message as text rather than as markup.
A code no variable has renders as an empty string, with nothing to say the code was wrong.

This directive takes no formatting at all. A parameter that is not in quotation marks runs to the next space, so {{customVar code=my_code|escape}} looks for a variable whose code is my_code|escape, finds none, and prints nothing.

variable.title: The {{trans}} directive
variable.summary: Prints a piece of text in the language of the store view the message is sent in.
variable.origin: The quoted text is looked up in the translations for the store view the message is sent in and printed. Parameters written after it fill the placeholders in the text: a parameter named var fills %var.

affordance.label: How to change the wording
affordance.step: The text between the quotation marks is both what is printed and the key the translation is looked up by. Changing it means any translation of the old wording no longer applies to it.
Translations come from the language pack of the store view's locale. Add or change the row for this text there, then flush the translation cache.

variable.caveat: The text has to be in quotation marks. When it is not, or the closing quotation mark is missing, the directive prints nothing at all rather than printing the text as written.

Everything after the first vertical bar inside the directive is read as formatting, so a message that contains a vertical bar of its own is cut in half - the remaining fragment has no closing quotation mark and the directive prints nothing.
Like {{var}}, a {{trans}} directive with no vertical bar in it is escaped as HTML, and any formatting name that is not escape or nl2br switches that off without a word.
When no translation exists for the store view's language the text is printed exactly as it was written, so an untranslated string and a missing dictionary look the same.

The value shown above is the translated text with its placeholders left standing. What fills them is supplied by the code that sends the message, not by the directive, so a recipient sees a value in each place where a per cent sign and a name appear here.

variable.title: The {{block}} directive
variable.summary: Renders a block of the storefront inside the message and prints its markup.
variable.origin: The class parameter names a block class to create, or the id parameter names a CMS block by its identifier. Every other parameter is set on the block as data before it is rendered, so a block can be told what to show.

affordance.label: How to change what it renders
affordance.step: What the block prints comes from its own template file. To change it, override that template in your theme rather than editing anything here.
To change what the block is given, change the parameters on the directive; each one is handed to the block as data under its own name.

variable.caveat: With neither a class nor an id parameter the directive prints nothing.
The output parameter names the method to call on the block. When it names a method the block does not have, the block is rendered normally instead, so a mistyped method name fails quietly.

variable.title: The {{layout}} directive
variable.summary: Builds a layout handle and prints the markup of the outermost block it produces.
variable.origin: The handle parameter names the layout handle to load. Any other parameter, apart from area, is set as data on every block the handle produces.

affordance.label: How to change what it renders
affordance.step: What the handle produces is decided by the layout XML files that declare it. Add or override that layout XML in your theme or module.
The area parameter decides which area the layout is built in. Leaving it out builds the frontend layout, which is what a message normally wants.

variable.caveat: The directive builds a complete layout for the handle, not a single block, so it is considerably more expensive to render than {{block}} and prints only the outermost block that comes out of it.

variable.title: The {{media}} directive
variable.summary: Prints the address of a file kept in the media directory.
variable.origin: The value of the url parameter is appended to the media base address of the store view the message is sent in. HTML entities in the parameter are decoded first, so an address written with & in it still comes out correct.

affordance.label: How to change the file
affordance.step: Put the file in the media directory - through the media gallery, or on the server - and write its path, relative to that directory, in the url parameter.

variable.caveat: The address is assembled from the text it is given and the file is never looked for, so a path with a typo in it produces a link that leads nowhere rather than an error.

variable.title: The {{store}} directive
variable.summary: Prints an address on the storefront of the store view the message is sent in.
variable.origin: The url parameter is the path the address is built for; an empty one gives the home page. A direct_url parameter is used as the path without any routing. Parameters whose name starts with _query_ become query-string parameters of the result.

affordance.label: How to change where it points
affordance.step: Change the url parameter to the path you want; it is written the way a storefront route is, without a leading slash.
To add something to the query string, add a parameter named _query_ followed by the name it should have, for instance _query_utm_source.

variable.caveat: The address is built for the store view the message is sent in, so the same directive produces different addresses in different store views.

variable.title: The {{protocol}} directive
variable.summary: Prints http or https, whichever the store view is currently being served over, or a complete address using it.
variable.origin: With no parameters the directive prints just the scheme. With a url parameter it prints the scheme, then ://, then the parameter. With both an http and an https parameter it prints whichever of the two matches. A store parameter chooses which store view to ask.
variable.caveat: When both an http and an https parameter are given, each really has to begin with its own scheme. If either does not, sending the message fails with an error instead of falling back to the other one.
A store parameter naming a store view that does not exist stops the message with an error rather than falling back to the current one.

variable.title: The {{css}} directive
variable.summary: Puts the contents of a stylesheet from the theme into the message, where the directive stands.
variable.origin: The file parameter names a file below the theme's web directory, or a file belonging to a module written as Magento_Sales::css/name.css. The file is compiled and its result replaces the directive.

affordance.label: How to change the stylesheet
affordance.step: Copy the stylesheet into your own theme, under web/css/ in the theme directory.
Edit the copy. A file in the theme takes precedence over the one the theme inherits.
Deploy static content so the change reaches the next message that is sent.

variable.caveat: In a plain-text template the directive produces nothing at all.

When the file is missing, fails to compile, or compiles to nothing, the directive leaves a CSS comment in the message rather than reporting an error, so the message still sends and simply arrives unstyled.
Without a file parameter the directive leaves a CSS comment saying so, in the message itself.

variable.title: The {{inlinecss}} directive
variable.summary: Applies a stylesheet to the message by writing the styles onto the elements themselves, which is what mail programs that ignore a stylesheet need. It prints nothing where it stands.
variable.origin: The file parameter names the stylesheet. The styles are applied once the whole message has been assembled, because inlining has to see the finished document, so the directive itself is replaced by nothing at the point where it is written.

affordance.label: How to change the stylesheet
affordance.step: Copy the stylesheet into your own theme, under web/css/ in the theme directory, and edit the copy.
Deploy static content so the change reaches the next message that is sent.

variable.caveat: In a plain-text template the directive does nothing at all.

In a template that is included by another one, the directive is left alone and the containing template deals with it, so moving it into a header or footer changes when it takes effect but not what it does.
Unlike {{css}}, a missing or empty file parameter stops the message with an error rather than leaving a comment behind.

variable.title: The {{template}} directive
variable.summary: Includes another email template, named indirectly by the configuration setting that holds it.
variable.origin: The config_path parameter names a configuration path, and the value found there is the template to include: a number when it is a template saved in the admin, or the code of one shipped by a module. The included template is rendered with the same variables as the one that includes it.

affordance.label: How to change what is included
affordance.step: The parameter names a configuration setting rather than a template, so what is included changes by changing that setting, not by editing the directive.
The header and footer of transactional messages are held at design/email/header_template and design/email/footer_template, which are chosen per store view in the design configuration.

variable.caveat: When the config_path parameter is missing, the words {Error in template processing} are printed into the message instead of the include failing.

variable.title: The {{depend}} directive
variable.summary: Keeps the text between it and its closing tag only when the variable it names has a value.
variable.origin: The name written after depend is read the same way a {{var}} path is. When it comes back empty the whole block is left out; otherwise the text inside it is rendered normally.

affordance.label: How to change the condition
affordance.step: Change the variable named after depend. It is a plain variable path - the same one you would write inside {{var}}.
Every {{depend}} needs a matching {{/depend}}. Without one the block is not recognised and the text around it is printed as written.

variable.caveat: There is no comparison here. The only question asked is whether the value is empty, so the directive cannot test a value against another value.

The block ends at the first {{/depend}} that follows it, so writing one {{depend}} inside another does not nest: the outer block ends at the inner one's closing tag and the remaining closing tag is left in the message.

variable.title: The {{if}} directive
variable.summary: Chooses between two pieces of text according to whether the variable it names has a value.
variable.origin: The name written after if is read the same way a {{var}} path is. When it has a value the text up to {{else}} is rendered; when it is empty the text after {{else}} is rendered, and nothing at all if there is no {{else}}.

affordance.label: How to change the condition
affordance.step: Change the variable named after if. It is a plain variable path - the same one you would write inside {{var}}.
Every {{if}} needs a matching {{/if}}; {{else}} between the two is optional and may appear once.

variable.caveat: There is no comparison and there is no chain of conditions. The only question asked is whether the value is empty, and there is no way to write "otherwise, if".
The block ends at the first {{/if}} that follows it, so one {{if}} written inside another does not nest.

variable.title: The {{for}} directive
variable.summary: Repeats the text between it and its closing tag once for every item of a list, such as the lines of an order.
variable.origin: It is written {{for item in order.items}}. The name before in is the name each item takes inside the block; the name after in is read the same way a {{var}} path is and has to come back as a list.

affordance.label: How to change what it repeats over
affordance.step: Change the name after in to another variable that holds a list. If it does not hold one, nothing is repeated.
Inside the block, write the name before in followed by a full stop and the value you want, for instance {{var item.name}}.

variable.caveat: When the name after in does not come back as a list, the directive is left in the message exactly as it was written, closing tag and all.

Inside the block, everything between the braces is read as a variable path and nothing else. A vertical bar becomes part of the name, so {{var item.name|escape}} matches nothing and prints an empty string - and, more seriously, values printed inside the block are not escaped the way the same directive outside the block would be.
Only variable paths are expanded inside the block. A {{depend}} or an {{if}} written inside it is not treated as a directive.
A counter is available inside the block: {{var loop.index}} gives the position of the current item, counting from zero.

variable.title: The {{view}} directive
variable.summary: Prints the address of a static file belonging to a theme or a module, such as an image.
variable.origin: The url parameter names the file and the directive prints the address it has been published at for the theme the message is rendered with.

affordance.label: How to change the file
affordance.step: A file belonging to the theme is written relative to the theme's web directory, for instance images/logo.png, and is replaced by putting your own copy at the same place in your theme.
A file belonging to a module has to be written with the module in front of it, as Magento_Sales::images/logo.png. Without that part it is looked for in the theme.
Deploy static content after replacing a file, so the published copy the address points at is the new one.

variable.caveat: The directive prints an address, never the file itself, so it belongs in the src attribute of an image rather than in the body of the message.

variable.title: Store country
variable.summary: The name of the country in the store's own address.
variable.origin: Stored in the configuration under Stores > Configuration > General > General > Store Information as the Country setting, which holds a country code rather than a name. Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::configDirective replaces that code with the country's name before printing it.
variable.caveat: What the message shows is not what is stored. The setting holds a country code and the message shows the country's name, so the two never look alike and the printed value cannot be typed back into the setting.
When no country is chosen the directive prints nothing at all, rather than printing a code or leaving the directive visible.
The Country setting is offered at the default and website scopes only. Every store view of a website therefore shows the same country, whatever the scope switcher in this editor is set to.

variable.title: Store region or state
variable.summary: The region or state in the store's own address.
variable.origin: Stored in the configuration under Stores > Configuration > General > General > Store Information as the Region/State setting, which accepts free text. Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::configDirective replaces the stored value with a region's name when it matches a region record, and prints it unchanged when it does not.
variable.caveat: What the message shows is not reliably what is stored: a value that matches a region record is replaced by that region's name, and one that does not is printed as it was typed. Which of the two happened is not visible from the message.

The formatted store address block is stricter than this directive. It shows the region only when the stored value matches a region record, so free text that matches none is printed here and yet missing from the address block.
The Region/State setting is offered at the default and website scopes only, so every store view of a website shows the same region.

variable.title: Store address block
variable.summary: The store's own postal address, already laid out over several lines.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate works the address out before the message is rendered and puts it on the store object under formatted_address. It is built by Magento\Store\Model\Information from the Store Information configuration group, laid out with the fixed five-line template in Magento\Store\Model\Address\Renderer, and its line breaks are then turned into br tags.
variable.caveat: The value contains br tags. With no formatting the directive escapes them and they appear in the message as text, which is why this one is normally written with the raw idiom.
The layout of the block is fixed in Magento and is not chosen per country. Changing it means replacing the address renderer's template in code; nothing in the admin does it.

The name, the first street line, the region and the country are printed whether or not they are set, so an unfilled one leaves a blank line. The second street line, the city and the postcode are left out when they are empty.
The last line is the country's name, not its code, and it is empty when no country is set. The region appears only when the Region/State setting matches a region record.

variable.title: Store address block, written as a method call
variable.summary: The store's own postal address, already laid out over several lines.
variable.origin: The brackets are not a method call: the path is read as a request for the formatted_address value held on the store object, which Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate puts there before the message is rendered. It is built by Magento\Store\Model\Information from the Store Information configuration group, laid out with the fixed five-line template in Magento\Store\Model\Address\Renderer, and its line breaks are then turned into br tags.
variable.caveat: {{var store.formatted_address}} prints exactly the same thing. Both spellings are read as the same value, and neither is more correct than the other.
The value contains br tags. With no formatting the directive escapes them and they appear in the message as text, which is why this one is normally written with the raw idiom.
The layout of the block is fixed in Magento and is not chosen per country. Changing it means replacing the address renderer's template in code; nothing in the admin does it.

The name, the first street line, the region and the country are printed whether or not they are set, so an unfilled one leaves a blank line. The second street line, the city and the postcode are left out when they are empty.

variable.title: Store name
variable.summary: The name of the store the message is sent for, as customers are meant to see it.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate puts it on the store object under frontend_name before the message is rendered. Magento\Store\Model\Store::getFrontendName reads the Store Name setting of the Store Information configuration group, and falls back to the name of the store the store view belongs to when that setting is empty.
variable.caveat: Clearing the Store Name setting does not empty this. When the setting has no value the name of the store the store view belongs to is printed instead, which is why a name often survives being deleted.
This is not the name a store view is listed under in Stores > All Stores. It is the Store Name configuration setting, with the store's name as a fallback, and the two are edited in different places.

variable.title: Store name, written as a method call
variable.summary: The name of the store the message is sent for, as customers are meant to see it.
variable.origin: The brackets are not a method call: the path is read as a request for the frontend_name value held on the store object, which Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate puts there before the message is rendered. It comes from the Store Name setting of the Store Information configuration group, falling back to the name of the store the store view belongs to when that setting is empty.
variable.caveat: {{var store.frontend_name}} prints exactly the same thing. Both spellings are read as the same value.
Clearing the Store Name setting does not empty this. When the setting has no value the name of the store the store view belongs to is printed instead.

variable.title: Store address of the shop, written as a method call
variable.summary: This does not print the address of the shop. On a standard installation it prints nothing at all.
variable.origin: A path inside {{var}} is never a method call. getBaseUrl() is read as a request for a base_url value held on the store object, and nothing puts one there while a message is being rendered, so the path comes back empty.

affordance.label: What to write instead
affordance.step: For a link into the shop, write {{store url=""}}, which builds the address for the store view the message is sent in. A path may be given instead of the empty string.
For the configured address itself, write {{config path="web/unsecure/base_url"}} or {{config path="web/secure/base_url"}}.

variable.caveat: Nothing reports this. The directive is replaced by an empty string, so a link written around it simply arrives with nothing in it.
The same is true of any other method spelled into a {{var}} path whose value nothing has put on the object first. Only the values the sending code assigned can be read.

variable.title: Store email address
variable.summary: The address a message offers the recipient to write back to.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables reads it from the configuration for the store view the message is sent in. Despite the general-sounding name it reads the Customer Support identity and nothing else.
variable.caveat: It is the Customer Support address. Changing the General Contact address, or the address a particular kind of message is sent from, leaves this value untouched.
It is not necessarily the address the message was sent from. Which identity sends a message is a separate setting on that message's own configuration page.

variable.title: Store phone number
variable.summary: The store's telephone number, as recorded in the store information.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables reads it from the configuration for the store view the message is sent in.
variable.caveat: The shipped templates wrap it in a depend directive, because an unset phone number would otherwise leave a sentence such as "or call us at" with nothing after it.

variable.title: Store opening hours
variable.summary: The store's opening hours, as recorded in the store information.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables reads it from the configuration for the store view the message is sent in.
variable.caveat: The field is free text, so whatever is typed there is what the message prints.

variable.title: The order
variable.summary: The order the message is about.
variable.origin: The sender puts the order record itself under this name. The invoice, shipment and credit memo senders pass the same record under the same name, so the order messages and the documents raised against an order all see it.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Orders and find the order the message is about.
Change the order there. The message reports whatever the order says at the moment it is sent; nothing in the template decides it.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to one family of messages does not exist in another. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
This is the order record rather than a piece of text. A template reads a field from it, as in order.increment_id, or passes it to another directive as $order.

variable.title: Order number
variable.summary: The order number the customer sees, such as 000000123.
variable.origin: Read from the order record the sender assigns. The invoice, shipment and credit memo messages carry the same order record, so the order number is available in those too.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The number is issued by the store's own numbering sequence when the order is placed, and cannot be edited afterwards.
Open Sales > Orders to find the order this number belongs to.

variable.title: Order record id
variable.summary: The database identifier of the order.
variable.origin: The sender assigns the order's own primary key alongside the order record.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The identifier is assigned by the database when the order is created and never changes.
Print order.increment_id instead when the message should show the customer their order number.

variable.caveat: This is not the order number on the customer's confirmation. It is an internal key and means nothing to a recipient.

variable.title: Shipping method description
variable.summary: The shipping method the customer chose, as it was worded when the order was placed.
variable.origin: Read from the order record the sender assigns. The wording is stored on the order at the time of purchase rather than looked up when the message is sent.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The description already on an existing order cannot be changed from the template.
To change what future orders record, adjust the carrier's method titles under Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods.

variable.caveat: An order with nothing to ship has no shipping method, so the value is empty.

variable.title: Customer name on the order
variable.summary: The name of the person who placed the order.
variable.origin: The sender calls getCustomerName() on the order and files the result under order_data. Every sales sender assembles the same order_data group, so the order, invoice, shipment and credit memo messages all carry it.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Orders, open the order, and change the name on the billing address.
For a registered customer, changing the name on the account under Customers > All Customers affects future orders, not orders already placed.

variable.title: Order status label
variable.summary: The status of the order in the wording shown to customers.
variable.origin: The sender calls getFrontendStatusLabel() on the order. That is the customer-facing label of the status rather than its internal code, and the two can differ.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Stores > Order Status to rename a status as customers see it.
To change which status an order is in, open it under Sales > Orders.

variable.caveat: Only the update and comment messages declare it. The confirmation message is sent when the order is placed, before any status change worth reporting.

variable.title: Note to the customer
variable.summary: The note an administrator wrote for the customer when the order was placed or edited.
variable.origin: The sender calls getEmailCustomerNote() on the order and files the result under order_data.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Orders, open the order, and edit the note that accompanies it.

variable.caveat: Most orders carry no such note, so the value is usually empty. The shipped template wraps it in a depend directive for that reason.

variable.title: Order has something to ship
variable.summary: A flag that is set when the order contains at least one item that needs delivering.
variable.origin: The sender calls getIsNotVirtual() on the order, which is the negation of the order's virtual flag, and files the result under order_data.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Whether an order is virtual follows from the products on it. Change the product types under Catalog > Products if future orders should be treated differently.

variable.caveat: It exists to be tested rather than printed. The shipped templates use it as the condition of a depend directive around the shipping sections.

variable.title: Order date
variable.summary: The date and time the order was placed, written out for reading.
variable.origin: The sender calls getCreatedAtFormatted(2) on the order, which formats the date and the time at medium length in the time zone configured for the order's store view.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The time zone comes from Stores > Configuration > General > Locale Options for the store view the order belongs to.
For a different wording, print a field of the order itself instead of this prepared string.

variable.caveat: Only the order sender prepares it. The invoice, shipment and credit memo senders do not, so in those messages it produces nothing.

variable.title: Shipping message
variable.summary: An extra line about delivery, printed under the shipping method.
variable.origin: The order confirmation template declares and prints this name, but no sender in Magento assigns it. It exists for an extension or an observer of the email_order_set_template_vars_before event to fill in.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Check whether any installed extension fills this name in. Nothing in Magento itself does.
If nothing fills it in, the directive can be removed from the template: it prints nothing either way.

variable.caveat: On a stock installation it is always empty, which is why the shipped template guards it with an if directive.

variable.title: Billing address block
variable.summary: The order's billing address, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: Every sales sender renders the order's billing address through the address renderer in its html layout and assigns the result under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: To change the address itself, open the order under Sales > Orders and edit its billing address.
To change how any address is laid out, open Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Address Templates and edit the HTML template.

variable.caveat: The html layout puts line breaks and a telephone link into the value, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped templates print it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Shipping address block
variable.summary: The order's delivery address, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: Every sales sender renders the order's shipping address through the address renderer in its html layout and assigns the result under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: To change the address itself, open the order under Sales > Orders and edit its shipping address.
To change how any address is laid out, open Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Address Templates and edit the HTML template.

variable.caveat: An order with nothing to ship has no shipping address, and the senders assign nothing at all in that case, so the value is empty.
The html layout puts line breaks and a telephone link into the value, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped templates print it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Payment details block
variable.summary: The payment method's own summary of how the order was paid for.
variable.origin: The order, invoice, shipment and credit memo senders ask the payment helper to render the payment method's information block for the order's store view, and assign the rendered block under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: What appears here is decided by the payment method. Its title comes from Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods.
For a different layout, override the payment method's information template in your own theme.

variable.caveat: The value is a rendered block of markup, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped templates print it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Comment sent with the document
variable.summary: The comment an administrator chose to send to the customer with this document.
variable.origin: The invoice, shipment and credit memo senders assign the document's customer note here, but only when the note was marked for sending; otherwise they assign an empty string. The order, invoice, shipment and credit memo comment senders assign the comment being sent directly.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open the order under Sales > Orders and add or edit the comment on the invoice, shipment or credit memo you are sending.
Tick the option that notifies the customer. Without it the senders assign an empty string and the message shows no comment.

variable.caveat: A comment that exists but was not marked for sending arrives as an empty value rather than as the comment.
The shipped templates print it escaped and then turn its line breaks into markup, so what the administrator typed is shown as text and its paragraphs survive.

variable.title: The invoice
variable.summary: The invoice the message is about.
variable.origin: The sender puts the invoice record itself under this name, beside the order it belongs to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Invoices and find the invoice the message is about.
The message reports whatever the invoice says at the moment it is sent; nothing in the template decides it.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to the invoice messages does not exist in another family. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
This is the invoice record rather than a piece of text. A template reads a field from it, as in invoice.increment_id, or passes it to another directive as $invoice.

variable.title: Invoice number
variable.summary: The invoice number the customer sees.
variable.origin: Read from the invoice record the sender assigns.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The number is issued when the invoice is raised and cannot be edited afterwards.

variable.title: Invoice record id
variable.summary: The database identifier of the invoice.
variable.origin: The sender assigns the invoice's own primary key alongside the invoice record.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The identifier is assigned by the database when the invoice is created and never changes.
Print invoice.increment_id instead when the message should show the customer their invoice number.

variable.caveat: It is an internal key and means nothing to a recipient. The shipped template passes it to the items grid rather than printing it.

variable.title: The shipment
variable.summary: The shipment the message is about.
variable.origin: The sender puts the shipment record itself under this name, beside the order it belongs to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Shipments and find the shipment the message is about.
The message reports whatever the shipment says at the moment it is sent, including its tracking numbers; nothing in the template decides it.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to the shipment messages does not exist in another family. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
This is the shipment record rather than a piece of text. A template reads a field from it, as in shipment.increment_id, or passes it to another directive as $shipment.

variable.title: Shipment number
variable.summary: The shipment number the customer sees.
variable.origin: Read from the shipment record the sender assigns.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The number is issued when the shipment is created and cannot be edited afterwards.

variable.title: Shipment record id
variable.summary: The database identifier of the shipment.
variable.origin: The sender assigns the shipment's own primary key alongside the shipment record.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The identifier is assigned by the database when the shipment is created and never changes.
Print shipment.increment_id instead when the message should show the customer their shipment number.

variable.caveat: It is an internal key and means nothing to a recipient.

variable.title: The credit memo
variable.summary: The credit memo the message is about.
variable.origin: The sender puts the credit memo record itself under this name, beside the order it belongs to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Sales > Credit Memos and find the credit memo the message is about.
The message reports whatever the credit memo says at the moment it is sent; nothing in the template decides it.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to the credit memo messages does not exist in another family. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
This is the credit memo record rather than a piece of text. A template reads a field from it, as in creditmemo.increment_id, or passes it to another directive as $creditmemo.

variable.title: Credit memo number
variable.summary: The credit memo number the customer sees.
variable.origin: Read from the credit memo record the sender assigns.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The number is issued when the credit memo is raised and cannot be edited afterwards.

variable.title: Credit memo record id
variable.summary: The database identifier of the credit memo.
variable.origin: The sender assigns the credit memo's own primary key alongside the credit memo record.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The identifier is assigned by the database when the credit memo is created and never changes.
Print creditmemo.increment_id instead when the message should show the customer their credit memo number.

variable.caveat: It is an internal key and means nothing to a recipient.

variable.title: The customer
variable.summary: The customer the message is addressed to.
variable.origin: For the account messages the notification service assigns the customer's record, with the assembled display name added to it under the name field. The wish list sharing message assigns the same kind of record. The payment failure message is the exception: there this name holds the customer's name as plain text, or the word Guest.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Customers > All Customers and edit the account the message is addressed to.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to the customer account messages does not exist in another family. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
In the account and wish list messages this is a record to read fields from, as in customer.name. In the payment failure message it is already the name, and reading a field from it produces nothing.

variable.title: Customer name
variable.summary: The customer's name, assembled the way the store is configured to show names.
variable.origin: The notification service builds the name with Magento\Customer\Helper\View::getCustomerName before sending, so any prefix, middle name and suffix that the store has made visible are included.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Customers > All Customers and edit the account's name fields.
Which name parts appear at all is decided by Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Name and Address Options.

variable.title: Customer email address
variable.summary: The address on the customer's account.
variable.origin: Read from the customer record the notification service assigns.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Customers > All Customers and edit the account's email address.

variable.caveat: On the message announcing a change of address, this is the address held on the account when the message is composed, which is not necessarily the address the message was delivered to.

variable.title: Link to the customer account page
variable.summary: The address of the store's customer account page.
variable.origin: The template model itself is available under the name this while a message is rendered, and getUrl builds a storefront address for the store view passed to it. The _nosid argument keeps the session identifier out of the link.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The host and path come from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.
To point somewhere else, change the route in the directive itself, keeping $store as the first argument so the link stays on the right store view.

variable.caveat: The shipped templates write this call with slightly different arguments in different messages, and each spelling is a separate entry here.

variable.title: Link for setting a password
variable.summary: A one-time address where the recipient can choose a password for their account.
variable.origin: The template model builds a storefront address for the store view and appends the customer's id together with the reset token held on their account, so the link only works for that customer.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: How long the link stays usable is set under Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Password Options.
The host and path come from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.

variable.caveat: The link only works while the account holds a reset token. Removing the token argument from the directive produces a link that cannot set a password.

variable.title: Subscription confirmation link
variable.summary: The address a new subscriber follows to confirm they asked to subscribe.
variable.origin: The subscriber model builds the link from the subscriber's confirmation code and assigns it under subscriber_data before sending the confirmation request.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The message is only sent at all when Stores > Configuration > Customers > Newsletter asks subscribers to confirm.
The host and path come from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so a name assigned to the confirmation request does not exist in the success or unsubscribe messages. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.

variable.title: Unsubscribe link
variable.summary: The address a subscriber follows to stop receiving the newsletter.
variable.origin: The queue builds the link from the subscriber's own record as it sends each copy of a queued newsletter, and assigns it under subscriber_data.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The host and path come from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.

variable.caveat: Only a newsletter sent from a queue carries it. The subscription confirmation, success and unsubscribe messages are sent by the subscriber model, which does not assign it, so there it produces nothing.

variable.title: Name given on the contact form
variable.summary: The name the visitor typed into the contact form.
variable.origin: The controller wraps the submitted form and passes it to the contact mailer, which assigns it under the name data. The form refuses to submit without a name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the visitor typed.
Where the message is sent is set under Stores > Configuration > General > Contacts.

variable.caveat: It is text typed by a stranger. It reaches the template exactly as submitted, so removing the escaping from this directive lets a visitor put markup into the message you receive.

The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so the names under data exist only in the contact form message. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.

variable.title: Email address given on the contact form
variable.summary: The address the visitor typed into the contact form.
variable.origin: The controller wraps the submitted form and passes it to the contact mailer, which assigns it under the name data and also sets it as the address a reply goes to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the visitor typed.

variable.caveat: The controller only checks that the value contains an at sign before accepting the form, so it is not necessarily a working address.
It is text typed by a stranger. It reaches the template exactly as submitted, so removing the escaping from this directive lets a visitor put markup into the message you receive.

variable.title: Telephone number given on the contact form
variable.summary: The telephone number the visitor typed into the contact form.
variable.origin: The controller wraps the submitted form and passes it to the contact mailer, which assigns it under the name data.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the visitor typed.

variable.caveat: The form is accepted without a telephone number, so this is frequently empty.
It is text typed by a stranger. It reaches the template exactly as submitted, so removing the escaping from this directive lets a visitor put markup into the message you receive.

variable.title: Message left on the contact form
variable.summary: What the visitor wrote in the contact form's message box.
variable.origin: The controller wraps the submitted form and passes it to the contact mailer, which assigns it under the name data. The form refuses to submit with an empty message.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the visitor typed.

variable.caveat: It is text typed by a stranger. It reaches the template exactly as submitted, so removing the escaping from this directive lets a visitor put markup into the message you receive.
Line breaks arrive as they were typed and are not turned into markup, so a long message runs together unless the directive is asked to convert them.

variable.title: Alerted products block
variable.summary: The list of products the alert is about, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: The alert model renders the products into a storefront block while emulating the recipient's store view, and assigns the rendered block under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The layout comes from the product alert block's own template. Override it in your own theme to change it.
Deploy static content so the change reaches the next alert that is sent.

variable.caveat: The value is a rendered block of markup, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped templates print it with the raw idiom.

The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so this name exists only in the product alert messages. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.

variable.title: Customer name
variable.summary: The name of the customer the message is about.
variable.origin: The alert model builds the name with Magento\Customer\Helper\View::getCustomerName and assigns it under this name. The wish list sharing message assigns the sharer's name the same way, in Magento\Wishlist\Controller\Index\Send.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Customers > All Customers and edit the account's name fields.
Which name parts appear at all is decided by Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Name and Address Options.

variable.caveat: In a product alert this is the recipient's name. In the wish list sharing message it is the name of the person who shared the list, not the recipient's.

variable.title: Link to the shared wish list
variable.summary: The address where the recipient can see the whole shared wish list.
variable.origin: The controller builds the link from the wish list's sharing code, so it opens that one list without the recipient signing in.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The host and path come from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so this name exists only in the wish list sharing message. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.

variable.title: Items block
variable.summary: The list of items the message is about, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: The wish list controller renders the list's items into a storefront block and assigns the rendered block under this name. The payment failure message assigns a different thing under the same name: Magento\Sales\Model\Service\PaymentFailuresService builds one line per basket item and joins them with line-break markup.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: In the wish list message the layout comes from the wish list email items block. Override its template in your own theme to change it.
In the payment failure message the wording is built in the sending code and cannot be changed from the template.

variable.caveat: The value carries markup in both messages, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped templates print it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Message from the sender
variable.summary: The note the person sharing the list or the product wrote to the recipient.
variable.origin: The wish list controller escapes what was typed and turns its line breaks into markup before assigning it, and appends the feed link when one was asked for. Magento\SendFriend\Model\SendFriend::send prepares the note on the share-a-product message exactly the same way.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the sender typed on the sharing form.
How long the note may be is set under Stores > Configuration > Customers > Wish List for the wish list, and under Catalog > Email to a Friend for the product share.

variable.caveat: The sending code has already made the text safe and converted its line breaks, which is why the shipped templates print it with the raw idiom. Escaping it a second time would show the line-break tags as text.
The sharing forms accept an empty note, so the shipped templates wrap it in a depend directive.

variable.title: Shared product name
variable.summary: The name of the product being shared.
variable.origin: The model reads the name from the product being shared and assigns it under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Catalog > Products and edit the product's name for the store view the message is sent in.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so the names in this set exist only in the share-a-product message. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.

variable.title: Shared product link
variable.summary: The address of the product being shared.
variable.origin: The model asks the product for its address in the current store and assigns it under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The path comes from the product's URL key, on the product's Search Engine Optimization section under Catalog > Products.
The host comes from the store view's base URL, under Stores > Configuration > General > Web.

variable.title: Shared product image
variable.summary: The address of the small image of the product being shared.
variable.origin: The model prepares the product's image in the size the share-a-product message asks for and assigns its address. When the product has no image of that role, the placeholder's address is assigned instead.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Catalog > Products and set the product's small image.
The stand-in used when there is no image is set under Stores > Configuration > Catalog > Catalog > Product Image Placeholders.

variable.caveat: It is never empty: without a product image the placeholder is used, so the message always shows a picture of some kind.

variable.title: Recipient name
variable.summary: The name of the person the shared product is being sent to.
variable.origin: The model takes the name from the sharing form, one per recipient, and assigns it under this name for that recipient's copy of the message.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the sender typed on the sharing form.

variable.caveat: The name is unusually plain, and no other message assigns it. Do not expect it to mean anything outside the share-a-product message.

variable.title: Recipient email address
variable.summary: The address the shared product is being sent to.
variable.origin: The model takes the address from the sharing form, one per recipient, and assigns it under this name for that recipient's copy of the message.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the sender typed on the sharing form.

variable.caveat: The name is unusually plain, and no other message assigns it. Do not expect it to mean anything outside the share-a-product message.

variable.title: Sharer name
variable.summary: The name of the person who shared the product.
variable.origin: The model escapes the name given on the sharing form and assigns it under this name. It also uses it as the name a reply to the message would go to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the sender typed on the sharing form.

variable.caveat: The value has already been made safe by the sending code, so the message shows it as text whatever the directive is asked to do.

variable.title: Sharer email address
variable.summary: The address of the person who shared the product.
variable.origin: The model escapes the address given on the sharing form and assigns it under this name. It also uses it as the address a reply to the message would go to.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Nothing in the administration decides this value; it is what the sender typed on the sharing form.

variable.caveat: The message is sent from the store's own General Contact identity, not from this address. Only a reply goes here.

variable.title: Why the payment failed
variable.summary: The explanation the payment attempt came back with.
variable.origin: The message that reached the checkout when the payment was refused is passed straight through to the template.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The wording comes from the payment method that refused the payment and cannot be changed from the template.

variable.caveat: The sending code decides which variables a message receives, so the names in this set exist only in the payment failure message. An unassigned name is not an error: Magento\Email\Model\Template\Filter::varDirective asks for the variable with an empty string as its fallback, so the directive quietly produces nothing at all.
The message goes to a member of staff rather than to the customer: the recipient is chosen under Stores > Configuration > Sales > Checkout > Payment Failed Emails.

variable.title: Where the payment was attempted
variable.summary: Which checkout the failed payment was made through.
variable.origin: The code that reports the failure names the checkout it happened in; the standard checkout reports itself as onepage.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The value is decided by the code reporting the failure and cannot be changed from the template.

variable.caveat: It is an internal name rather than a phrase prepared for reading, and it is not translated.

variable.title: Address on the basket
variable.summary: The email address recorded on the basket the payment failed for.
variable.origin: Read from the billing address of the basket.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The value comes from what the shopper entered in the checkout and cannot be changed from the template.

variable.title: When the message was composed
variable.summary: The date and time written into the payment failure message.
variable.origin: The sending code formats the current moment at medium date and time length. Despite the template's label it is the moment the message is composed, not the moment the payment was attempted.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The time zone and the wording follow the locale settings under Stores > Configuration > General > Locale Options.

variable.caveat: It is the time the message was put together. When failures are reported in a batch, it is not the time of the payment attempt.

variable.title: Payment method title
variable.summary: The name of the payment method the shopper tried to pay with.
variable.origin: The sending code reads the title configured for the method the basket was using.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Stores > Configuration > Sales > Payment Methods and edit the method's title.

variable.caveat: When the basket never got as far as choosing a method, there is no title to read and the value is empty.

variable.title: Delivery method title
variable.summary: The name of the delivery method chosen on the basket.
variable.origin: The sending code takes the carrier from the basket's shipping method and reads that carrier's configured title.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: Open Stores > Configuration > Sales > Delivery Methods and edit the carrier's title.

variable.caveat: A basket with nothing to deliver has no method, so the value is empty. The shipped template wraps the delivery section in a depend directive on it.

variable.title: Basket total
variable.summary: The value of the basket the payment failed for.
variable.origin: The sending code joins the basket's store currency code and its grand total into one string.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: The wording is built in the sending code and cannot be changed from the template.

variable.caveat: The amount is not formatted for the locale: it is the currency code, a space, and the number as it is stored, so it can carry more decimal places than a price normally shows.

variable.title: Billing address block on the basket
variable.summary: The billing address entered in the checkout, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: The sending code formats the basket's billing address in the html layout and assigns the result under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: To change how any address is laid out, open Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Address Templates and edit the HTML template.

variable.caveat: The html layout puts line breaks and a telephone link into the value, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped template prints it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Delivery address block on the basket
variable.summary: The delivery address entered in the checkout, laid out ready to print.
variable.origin: The sending code formats the basket's shipping address in the html layout and assigns the result under this name.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: To change how any address is laid out, open Stores > Configuration > Customers > Customer Configuration > Address Templates and edit the HTML template.

variable.caveat: The html layout puts line breaks and a telephone link into the value, so a directive that escapes it shows the tags as text. The shipped template prints it with the raw idiom.

variable.title: Email logo image
variable.summary: The address of the picture shown at the top of the message.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::getLogoUrl looks for the file named in the design configuration under the media directory and builds its address. When no file is configured, or the configured file is missing, it falls back to the logo that ships with the current theme.
variable.caveat: The setting is Logo Image, in the Transactional Emails section of a design configuration record.
Design configuration is kept per scope, and the list shows one row for the default, one for each website and one for each store view. Open the row for the store view the message is sent in.
It is never empty. Without an uploaded file the theme's own logo is used, so a message always shows a picture.

variable.title: Email logo alternative text
variable.summary: The words shown in place of the logo when the picture cannot be loaded.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::getLogoAlt reads the design configuration and, when nothing is set there, falls back to the store view's frontend name.
variable.caveat: The setting is Logo Image Alt, in the Transactional Emails section of a design configuration record.
Leaving it blank does not produce a blank: the store view's name is used instead.
The design configuration form refuses a value containing tags, so this is always plain text.

variable.title: Email logo width
variable.summary: How wide the logo is drawn, in pixels.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables reads the design configuration for the store view the message is sent in. There is no fallback in the code.
variable.caveat: The setting is Logo Width, in the Transactional Emails section of a design configuration record.
The shipped header does the falling back itself: when nothing is set it draws the logo 180 pixels wide.
The design configuration form accepts digits only, so the number is written without a unit.

variable.title: Email logo height
variable.summary: How tall the logo is drawn, in pixels.
variable.origin: Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate::addEmailVariables reads the design configuration for the store view the message is sent in. There is no fallback in the code.
variable.caveat: The setting is Logo Height, in the Transactional Emails section of a design configuration record.
Unlike the width, the shipped header sets no height at all when nothing is configured; the picture keeps its own proportions.
The design configuration form accepts digits only, so the number is written without a unit.

variable.title: Template styles
variable.summary: The style rules a message carries of its own, printed inside the header's style block.
variable.origin: For a template held in a file, the rules come from a styles annotation at the top of that file, which Magento\Email\Model\AbstractTemplate strips out while loading it. For a template saved in the administration, they come from that template's own Template Styles field.

affordance.label: How to change this
affordance.step: For a template saved in the administration, edit its Template Styles field under Marketing > Email Templates.
For a template held in a file, edit the styles annotation at the top of that file, in your own theme rather than in the module it came from.

variable.caveat: The value is a block of style rules, so a directive that escapes it shows them as text inside the message. The shipped header prints it with the raw idiom.
A plain-text message is not given the value at all, so there the directive produces nothing.

The header is included by the message around it and receives that message's variables, so what it prints are the message's own style rules. The header's own rules are only used when the message above it has none.
